model: Squeeze-out special situation: compensation-anchored deal weighting (corporate_action) over a standalone owner-FCF going-concern DCF (engine route, deal-fails leg)

inputs.share_count_basis: 207,640,330 shares outstanding at 2025-12-31 (207,900,000 issued less 259,670 treasury), FY2025 AR line ~1046 / note 20. Includes the 18.9m new shares issued to XRG on 2025-12-10 in the EUR 1.17bn capital increase; the cash from that raise sits inside net financial debt, so count and bridge are on the same post-raise basis. No equity-settled awards, so basic = diluted. Held flat.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 AR compensation report (line ~12069): the Prisma LTI is cash-based (TSR/EVA metrics, paid in cash, no shares issued); its cost is already inside personnel expense and OCF. No equity-settled SBC -> SBC-zero filer, house and street bases coincide.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-23T15:35:16Z (Xetra regular-session close, Friday; latest available print on 2026-10-25)
inputs.wacc_rationale: EUR flows, EUR rate. 10y Bund ~2.7% + beta ~1.2 x 5.5% ERP -> cost of equity ~9.3%; after-tax cost of debt ~3.0% (Baa2, 0.875-4.75% coupons); ~20% debt weight at the pre-deal market value -> WACC ~8.0%. Covestro's own disclosed WACC is 7.3% (2025) / 6.8% (2026 planning); the house rate is deliberately above it. Same WACC in every scenario: cyclical risk is charged in the bear flows, not in the rate (adaptations 7f).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost. Lease cash = principal EUR 161m (FY2025 AR line 3116) + interest ~EUR 28m (est. ~4% on the EUR 674m liability) = ~EUR 189m = 1.45% of revenue, deducted via lease_cost_pct_path. Lease liabilities (EUR 674m) EXCLUDED from net debt. D&A path is ex right-of-use depreciation (EUR 184m) and ex impairments (EUR 226m) so the lease is not charged twice in cash-tax EBIT.
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI is immaterial (EUR 18m equity, mainly Covestro Eternal Resins (Kunshan)); deducted once at book in equity_bridge, flows are consolidated.
inputs.net_debt_basis: Covestro's own net financial debt EUR 1,796m (FY2025 AR lines 3120-3134) less lease liabilities EUR 674m = EUR 1,122m. total_debt 2,438 = bonds 1,494 + bank liabilities 967 + other 1 + FX-forward liabilities 5 - FX-forward receivables 29. cash 1,316 = cash and equivalents 648 + current financial assets (short-term bank deposits, money-market funds) 668 -- mostly the December 2025 capital-increase proceeds.
inputs.notes: MODEL CHOICE (dcf-methods routing table): 'Live takeover, scheme, strategic review -> deal-completes vs deal-breaks weighting, not three growth scenarios'. Covestro is in a German squeeze-out (sec. 327a AktG): XRG (ADNOC) holds 96.16%, the transfer resolution passed at the 2026-05-19 AGM, cash compensation is fixed at EUR 59.46/share and is secured by a mandatory bank guarantee (sec. 327b(3) AktG). Registration in the commercial register -- the step that transfers the shares -- was not confirmed as of 2026-10-24, which five months after the AGM most likely means annulment actions and a release proceeding (Freigabeverfahren) are pending. A minority holder cannot keep the shares: on registration they convert by law into the EUR 59.46 claim plus a pro-rata share of any later appraisal (Spruchverfahren) uplift. So the ACTIONABLE value is corporate_action.deal_weighted_iv. The three-scenario owner-FCF DCF built by the engine below is the deal-FAILS leg (weight 2%) and the fundamental cross-check on whether EUR 59.46 is a fair price for the business; it is NOT a value a minority holder can realise. probability_weighted.weighted_iv is therefore the standalone going-concern value, following the EZJ.L (Apollo scheme) precedent for this folder; read corporate_action.deal_weighted_iv for the decision. Lease treatment (B). SBC-zero (cash LTI) -> band_position null. Buybacks: none since FY2023 (EUR 49m); none expected under XRG. ANCHOR STALENESS: the latest extracted filing is the FY2025 annual (balance sheet 2025-12-31); Q1/H1/Q3 2026 reports are not in Extracted/. This barely matters for the decision (the going-concern leg carries 2% weight) but net debt and FY2026 run-rate should be refreshed if the deal-fails leg ever becomes live. owner FCF: last_fcf = reported FOCF -283 (OCF 487 - capex 770; SBC 0; interest income not stripped because Covestro is net debt). On the lease-(B) basis the FY2025 unlevered owner FCF is ~-472 (-283 - 161 principal - ~28 lease interest); FY0 was a trough year with EUR 226m impairments, EUR 149m STRONG restructuring cost and a Dormagen fire, not a base to carry forward -- the forward build is from components.

equity_bridge.item: Provisions for pensions and other post-employment benefits
equity_bridge.note: FY2025 AR balance sheet line 13258 (2024: 387). Pre-tax, at book.

equity_bridge.item: Cash taxes paid in group-loss years (PV, FY2026-FY2028)
equity_bridge.note: The engine taxes max(0, EBIT) only, but Covestro paid EUR 192m cash tax on a EUR -347m group EBIT in FY2025 (profitable regions, minimum taxes; FY2025 AR line 3026). Estimated excess over the engine's charge: ~170 (FY26) + ~100 (FY27) + ~50 (FY28) = 320 nominal, ~285 PV at 8%. German loss carry-forwards that might later offset are ignored (conservative).

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: long-run nominal volume+price growth for a mid-cycle polymers producer; equity 5yr CAGR (4.53%) is inflated by the EUR 1.15bn December 2025 capital increase (ex-raise ~0.85%), and revenue CAGRs are cycle-endpoint artefacts (FY2022 peak pricing, FY2020 COVID trough)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 4.53% vs revenue 5yr 3.87% is within 30%, but only because of the XRG capital raise; ex-raise equity grew 0.85%/yr. EPS CAGRs undefined (FY2025 EPS -3.39, FY2022 -1.42, FY2020 2.48). FCF CAGRs undefined (FY2025 FOCF -283).
historical_growth.notes: Reported FOCF FY2016-FY2025: 1,367 / 1,843 / 1,669 / 473 / 530 / 1,429 / 138 / 232 / 89 / -283; 10-year average ~750 before lease principal (post-IFRS 16) and interest. SBC is zero (cash LTI), so owner FCF and reported FCF coincide apart from the lease treatment; there is no SBC-vs-cash-flow divergence to flag. EBITDA margin 2015-2025: 11.7 / 16.9 / 24.3 / 21.9 / 12.9 / 13.7 / 19.4 / 9.0 / 7.5 / 7.6 / 5.7% (decade mean ~13.7%, inflated by the 2017-18 and 2021 MDI price spikes).

base.narrative: Trough-then-partial-recovery. FY2026 matches guidance (EBITDA 'around prior year' EUR 740m, sales slightly lower on price and FX). STRONG reaches its EUR 400m run-rate by 2028 and Chinese MDI/PC overcapacity is slowly absorbed, taking the EBITDA margin to 13% by 2032 -- close to the 13.7% decade mean but with no 2017-18/2021-style price spikes, because Wanhua-led Chinese capacity is structural, not cyclical.

bull.narrative: Classic cycle recovery plus the XRG platform. Chinese capacity additions pause and Western rationalisation (closures at BASF/Dow/Covestro's own sites) tightens MDI and PC; auto and construction recover from 2027; the full EUR 400m STRONG saving drops through; Antwerp, Zhuhai TPU and Newark capacity add specialty volume. EBITDA margin returns to 16% -- around the 2016 level, still below the 2017-18 and 2021 peaks.

bear.narrative: Structural de-rating of European commodity polymers. Chinese MDI/PC overcapacity persists for the decade, EU energy costs stay above US/Middle East peers, and US tariffs plus anti-dumping fights fragment trade. Savings are competed away in price; EBITDA margin recovers only to 9% (the FY2022 level) and capex is held near maintenance.

scenario_narratives.base: Going-concern base (deal-fails leg only): FY2026 EBITDA ~EUR 740m per guidance, gradual absorption of Chinese MDI/polycarbonate overcapacity, STRONG's EUR 400m saving by 2028, EBITDA margin to 13% by 2032 (decade mean ex price spikes). Axes: MDI/PC spread vs Chinese capacity, European auto/construction volume, EU energy cost.
scenario_narratives.bull: Going-concern bull: cyclical recovery from 2027 as Western capacity closes and Chinese additions pause; specialty capacity (Antwerp, Zhuhai TPU, Newark) ramps; margin back to ~16%, the 2016 level. Upside accrues to XRG, not to minority holders, under the squeeze-out.
scenario_narratives.bear: Going-concern bear: Chinese overcapacity is permanent, EU energy disadvantage persists, tariffs fragment trade; margin recovers only to 9% and capex is starved toward maintenance.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: These weights apply to the STANDALONE going-concern DCF only (the deal-fails leg). Bear 25% (above the 15% default): trough of a deep cycle with an unresolved structural Chinese overcapacity question and a European energy-cost handicap. Bull 25% (below the 35% default): it needs a cycle turn, Western capacity exits and specialty ramp-ups to coincide. Base 50%. With the squeeze-out live, the actionable number is corporate_action.deal_weighted_iv, which gives this standalone value only a 2% weight. NOTE: weighted_iv is the STANDALONE (deal-fails) value; corporate_action.deal_weighted_iv (EUR 59.25) is the decision value.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Covestro is not valued here as an operating equity. XRG (ADNOC) owns 96.16% and the AGM has approved a statutory squeeze-out at EUR 59.46 cash per share, backed by a bank guarantee; once the resolution is registered every remaining share is transferred by law. A minority holder's outcome is therefore a fixed-amount, guaranteed cash claim plus a free option on a court-ordered increase (Spruchverfahren), not a share of future Covestro cash flows. The headline decision value is corporate_action.deal_weighted_iv: P(registration) x [PV of EUR 59.46 at a near-risk-free rate + expected PV of an appraisal uplift] + P(failure) x standalone DCF. The owner-FCF DCF below (engine output, probability_weighted.weighted_iv) is kept for two reasons: it is the value in the improbable deal-fails path, and it answers whether EUR 59.46 is fair for the business. On house assumptions it is far below EUR 59.46 -- at the trough of the chemicals cycle, with structural Chinese overcapacity, a 12x terminal cap and 8% WACC, the going-concern value per share is a fraction of the compensation -- so the compensation is generous relative to a conservative fundamental view, and the only plausible source of extra value is the appraisal proceeding, which courts decide on an IDW S1 earnings value from management's own plan and on the 3-month pre-announcement VWAP floor, not on house assumptions.
key_risks_to_valuation: Timing: registration not confirmed as of 2026-10-24; pending annulment actions / Freigabeverfahren could push payment into H2 2027 or later. Each extra year costs ~2.5-3% of PV on the claim (no statutory interest accrues until registration is published).

Squeeze-out failure (modelled at 2%): an annulment action that succeeds and is not overridden by a release order would leave minorities in a 96%-controlled, General-Standard-listed, illiquid company whose going-concern value on house assumptions is far below the compensation.

Appraisal (Spruchverfahren) upside is uncertain in probability, size and timing (typically 3-7 years); the EUR 62 voluntary offer is a commonly-argued reference point but not a legal floor for squeeze-out compensation.
Price above compensation: at EUR 60.20 a buyer today pays more than the guaranteed cash amount and depends on the appraisal for any return.
Standalone DCF is terminal-heavy and trough-anchored; it is sensitive to the mature EBITDA margin (13% base) and the 12x terminal cap.
Stale operating anchors: no 2026 interim filings in the folder (latest balance sheet 2025-12-31).

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (Xetra, EUR). Yahoo now serves only post-segment-change bars for this symbol, so the pre-announcement 3-month VWAP (the Spruchverfahren floor reference) could not be reconstructed.
data_sources.financials: Covestro Annual Report FY2025 (Extracted/1COV.DE_Annual_FY2025.txt): key data p.1, net financial debt table lines 3120-3134, cash flows lines 3060-3118, forecast lines 3901-3943, equity and share count lines 1035-1046 and 16406-16482, right-of-use assets lines 15893-15906; Metrics.csv FY2014-FY2025 history.
data_sources.qualitative: 1COV.DE_Analysis.json (special_situation_notice, recent_developments, guidance) for the XRG takeover, the squeeze-out request, the EUR 59.46 compensation and the 2026-05-19 AGM resolution.

corporate_action.status: LIVE statutory squeeze-out (sec. 327a ff. AktG), resolution approved, registration pending -- the share price is pinned to the cash compensation, not to fundamentals. Re-check registration status before reusing any number in this file; once the resolution is registered the shares are transferred and this ticker should be pulled.
corporate_action.type: Squeeze-out of minority shareholders by the 96.16% majority holder for cash compensation
corporate_action.acquirer: XRG P.J.S.C. (ADNOC's international investment arm) via ADNOC International Germany Holding AG. Takeover closed 2025-12-10 after a EUR 62/share voluntary offer plus a EUR 1.17bn capital increase (18.9m new shares) subscribed by XRG.
corporate_action.compensation_basis: Set by XRG on an IDW S1 valuation reviewed by a court-appointed auditor, with a PwC fairness opinion (per Analysis.json); below the EUR 62 voluntary offer price. Secured by a mandatory bank guarantee (sec. 327b(3) AktG), so the claim carries bank credit risk, not Covestro risk.
corporate_action.milestones: Squeeze-out requested ~2026-03; Prime Standard exit / move to General Standard 2026-05-05; AGM transfer resolution approved 2026-05-19 (XRG at 96.16%); commercial-register entry NOT confirmed as of 2026-10-24.
corporate_action.registration_pending_reading: Five months between resolution and registration is longer than an unchallenged squeeze-out takes, which most likely means annulment actions (Anfechtungsklagen) were filed and a release proceeding (Freigabeverfahren, sec. 327e(2) with 319(6) AktG) is running. Release orders are granted in the large majority of cases and typically within months; the challenge delays the payment rather than threatening it.
corporate_action.claim_discount_rate_rationale: A fixed EUR amount backed by a bank guarantee: EUR short rate (~2%) plus a small timing/credit spread, not Covestro's cost of equity. Statutory interest (base rate + 5pp) only starts at publication of registration, and payment follows promptly, so it is ignored for the main claim.

appraisal_option.mechanism: Any shareholder may apply for a Spruchverfahren within three months of registration; an increase ordered by the court (or settled) applies to ALL squeezed-out shareholders, applicants or not, with statutory interest at the base rate + 5pp from registration.
appraisal_option.rationale: 35% x 8%: arguments for an uplift are the EUR 62 price XRG paid in the voluntary offer five months earlier and a trough-year planning base; against them, the voluntary offer price is not a legal floor for squeeze-out compensation, the 3-month pre-announcement VWAP floor (DAT/Altana-Stollwerck) appears to be respected (the stock traded around EUR 59-61), and this folder's own going-concern DCF sits far below EUR 59.46. The pre-announcement VWAP could not be reconstructed from Yahoo (only post-segment-change bars are served) -- if it proves to be above EUR 59.46 the uplift probability should rise materially.

corporate_action.probability_rationale: 98%. XRG is above the 95% threshold (96.16%), the resolution is passed, the compensation is bank-guaranteed, and German courts grant release orders in the large majority of challenged squeeze-outs. The residual 2% is an annulment action that succeeds and is not overridden, after which XRG would almost certainly re-run the process -- so even the fail leg is more delay than loss in practice; it is valued conservatively at the standalone DCF.
corporate_action.deal_breaks_value_basis: probability_weighted.weighted_iv -- the standalone three-scenario owner-FCF DCF in this file (bear 25% / base 50% / bull 25%; base 18.29, bull 36.46, bear -1.86). The bear case is negative at the equity level (EV < net debt + pensions + bridge): at FY2022-25-like margins the business does not earn its capex. Limited liability floors a holder at zero; the negative value is left unfloored as the engine's finding and carries 0.5% effective weight.
corporate_action.deal_weighted_iv_formula: P x [PV(59.46 at 3% over 0.5y) + E[PV appraisal uplift]] + (1-P) x standalone weighted IV = 0.98 x (58.59 + 1.50) + 0.02 x 17.80
corporate_action.deal_weighted_entry_formula: P x [PV(59.46 at 15% over 0.5y) + E[appraisal PV at 15%]] + (1-P) x standalone weighted entry price = 0.98 x (55.45 + 1.13) + 0.02 x 3.57
corporate_action.market_implied: At EUR 60.20 the market pays EUR 1.61 over the PV of the guaranteed EUR 59.46 claim (and EUR 0.74 over its face value). Solving 60.20 = 0.98 x (58.59 + X) + 0.02 x 17.80 gives an implied appraisal value X ~ EUR 2.48/share, ~1.6x this file's estimate -- equivalently, the market is pricing either a faster payment or a ~10-12% uplift at ~50% odds.
corporate_action.reading: The actionable value is deal_weighted_iv EUR 59.25, not probability_weighted.weighted_iv (17.80, the going-concern value in the 2% fail path). Price EUR 60.20 is ~1.6% above the deal value and ~8% above the 15%-hurdle entry of EUR 55.52: a buyer today accepts a negative spread on the guaranteed cash and is paying for the appraisal option. For an existing holder the decision is mechanical -- the shares will be exchanged for EUR 59.46 plus any court-ordered top-up regardless of what they do; selling in the market at EUR 60.20 now captures ~EUR 0.98 more than the PV of the guaranteed amount (about equal to this file's appraisal estimate, so roughly a wash, with the sale removing timing and litigation risk). Not an opportunity for a 15%-hurdle investor. The going-concern DCF says EUR 59.46 is a generous price for the business on house assumptions -- the minority is being bought out at a multiple of trough-cycle fundamental value.
